messages:
maya: Heads-up: SA warm-pool bootstrap failures starting ~04:05 UTC. Nodes keep retrying decrypt to the keystore and eventually timeout. Warm-pool kept spawning new nodes -> large GPU churn.

jorge: any obvious error from the node agent?

maya: snippet from node-agent logs: 
```
[2026-03-21T04:06:11Z] keystore: decrypt request failed: AccessDeniedException: "Caller does not satisfy IAM condition"
[2026-03-21T04:06:11Z] bootstrap: attestation failed, aborting
```
Also seeing Keystore audit logs: iam:SimulateDenied with condition "resource.tags.compliance == 'enabled'".

ops-bot: Alert: 46 nodes in south-america-1 failed bootstrap >3m (INVPROC-2916). Warm-pool growth rate high.

keith: Wait, security pushed an IAM condition for keystore cross-account assume-role last night to enforce vpc-tag-based scoping. Did SA subnets get the new tag?

maya: Checked — SA prod subnets are missing the tag (we missed onboarding script change). New tag landed in policy at 01:20. Nodes launched post-01:20 cannot decrypt.

finance-watch: Projection: if warm-pool keeps retrying another hour we could bill ~1.1k GPU-minutes (~$1.6k). Recommend immediate mitigation.

jorge: Mitigation options: A) tag subnets with compliance=enabled (fast) B) add a short-lived IAM exception allowing keystore assume from SA role C) pause warm-pool autoscaling. Do in what order?

keith: Prefer A then C then B as fallback. Tagging is lowest blast radius. I can patch infra templates but need an immediate manual tag to stop the bleeding.

maya: I'll run a targeted tag now for the three affected subnets and pause warm-pool autoscaling. Command: ``aws ec2 create-tags --resources subnet-0a1b2c3d subnet-0e4f5g6h --tags Key=compliance,Value=enabled --region south-america-1``

jorge: I added a short-lived scaling policy hold: warm-pool.max-size set to current to prevent further churn (15m).

maya: tagging applied. Keystore audit logs now show Acceptance for decrypt requests from new instances.

ops-bot: Note: INVPROC-2916 updated with remediation steps and owners.

keith: After tagging, we still have ~30 nodes in a failed state. Recommend requeueing their bootstrap and forcing a small batch restart to clear backoff. I'll run rolling restart on 10 at a time.

maya: kicking off restart batch 1/3. Watching agent logs.

jorge: also plan to open a follow-up: 1) update onboarding terraform to ensure subnet tags are present 2) add presubmit e2e that tests keystore assume with tag conditions 3) update runbook: if IAM condition changes, notify eng-sre and add quick rollback steps. I'll own the onboarding change.

finance-watch: cost watch: after tagging + pause, GPU churn stopped, projected cost delta down to ~$120 for the incident window.

keith: long-term: security and infra should coordinate on policy deploy ordering (policy-first vs infra-first). We should maybe gate IAM condition rollouts with a branch that verifies resource tags exist.

maya: agreed. For now incident closed to monitoring; kept INVPROC-2916 open for RCA. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
